\section{Design requirements and measured comparison}

The two circuits implement single-balanced downconversion at the assignment RF/LO/IF frequencies. The results below compare an active current-switching mixer and a passive switching mixer simulated in Cadence Spectre from native Virtuoso schematics through ADE.\cite{hw09,razavi2012}\footnote{All figures were exported from the native Cadence GUI in day mode because the default night-mode exports were difficult to read.}

Constraint & Implemented condition \\
\midrule
Technology / supply & NCSU 45 nm CMOS; $V_{DD}=1.0\,\mathrm{V}$; installed minimum $L=50\,\mathrm{nm}$ \\
RF / LO / IF & \ensuremath{5.8} / \ensuremath{5.6} GHz / \ensuremath{200} MHz \\
LO constraint & Each leg: \ensuremath{0.4}, \ensuremath{0.4} Vpp (active/passive); differential: \ensuremath{0.8}, \ensuremath{0.8} Vpp. Both are strictly below 1 Vpp. \\
Source / load & $R_s=50.0\,\Omega$; equal branch loads; $C_L=10.0\,\mathrm{fF}$ per output. \\
\bottomrule

\end{center}

The active circuit provides \ensuremath{8.573} dB voltage gain and \ensuremath{1.584} dB power gain at \ensuremath{0.6851} mW core power. The passive circuit has \ensuremath{5.975} dB voltage loss and \ensuremath{12.96} dB transducer power loss. Its zero core DC power excludes the ideal external LO driver. Loaded SSB NF is \ensuremath{11.15} / \ensuremath{16.69} dB (active/passive).

The measured IIP3 values are \ensuremath{-2.718} / \ensuremath{-5.472} dBm; active has the higher measured value. Compression and intermodulation are evaluated separately, with the uncertainty/brackets shown below.

The measured input P1dB values are \ensuremath{-15.55} / \ensuremath{-15.08} dBm; passive has the higher measured value. Compression and intermodulation are evaluated separately, with the uncertainty/brackets shown below.
